questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Firstly, Australian National University was and is still a globally highly ranked university within my field (political science), which was one of the primary aspects in choosing my study destination. Secondly, ANU is located in an English-speak country, which was another deciding factor when considering the expected quality of learning at the university. Thirdly, ANU provides a student housing guarantee, which was another requirement when choosing my study destination, as many university cities face challenging housing crises.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy (all things considered) to acquire the needed information upon arrival, as ANU have a very accessible and helpful administrative team. They replied quickly to my inquiries and were ready to find solutions to any problems I encountered.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Prior to arrival, it was possible to attend two online webinars at ANU to prepare for our exchange stay. Upon arrival, there was an Orientation Week, during which there were information sessions, stands, and various offers for exchange and international students especially.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I encourage participation in O-week.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: ANU has very many on-campus housing options, which differ depending on price (some are affordable, others are not) and who lives there (undergrad, grad / PhD, or mixed). They provide a housing guarantee to all international and exchange students, if housing applications are submitted before the deadline (and there are usually left-over spots after deadline as well). They have a useful online service, where you can compare the different houses and housing options.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Some student housing was non-catered, catered, or flexi-catered. The non-catered often have a private or shared kitchen available for cooking.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: For me, it was a great way to make friends and expand my network upon arrival. As a grad student, I stayed in a house only for grad or PhD students, which I really enjoyed, as the other were much closer to me in age than in the mixed housing options.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When the registration period opens, you can register online for courses. It is a good idea to register when it opens to ensure a spot; however, it was not nearly as competitive as the last time I went on exchange. NB! You need a pre-approval from your home institution for all the courses you want to register for.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an online guide which was very helpful. Email correspondence was also quick and somewhat efficient.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do your research on courses in advance and have a list of alternative courses ready (with pre-approvals from the home institution), in case a course you want is dropped for the term.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses varied somewhat, often according to the skills of the course convenor. However, I often found that the level at KU is higher than the level of classes internationally, and this was also the case for ANU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A shorter syllabus than at KU and multiple assessment pieces throughout the semester. Participation was also graded in all classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 1) Australian Environmental Policy. 2) From Family to Family-State: Social Power in China. 3) Introduction to Humanitarian Action. 4) Revolution, Rebellion, Riot: Unruly Politics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend "Revolution, Rebellion, Riot: Unruly Politics" because the professor is incredible, the class sessions are taught in a deliberative way that promotes independent thought and co-learning, and the class comprises creative elements that are both fun and great for learning in a different way.

I would also recommend "Australian Environmental Policy" as the professor is both nice and knowledgeable, and the course provides an alternative approach to public policy analysis and takes up some interesting (and often complex) cases of public policy whilst providing a great amount of background information on Australian history, politics, and culture.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think i encountered any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The visa was really expensive! While supermarket prices are comparable to Denmark, eating out is less expensive. Also note that there is a mandatory health insurance.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Did a weakly fitness class at the on-campus gym which was a lot of fun.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many different clubs, societies, and athletic activities. All can be found at the university website or Instagram.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The self-defense short-course and boxing class at ANU sport was great fun and a great opportunity to learn.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Canberra is a bit boring itself, but it is easy to take the bus to Sydney or the train to Melbourne. Otherwise rent a car and check out the nature surrounding Canberra or the coast.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy - unique Aussie culture but still a mix between British and American culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Kitchen cleaning habits in my dorm.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Aussie openness, kindness, and laid-back approach.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Apply for funding!
2) Live in an on-campus accommodation.
3) Participate in O-week.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I opened an Australian bank account which was both easy and useful. And if you have a driver's license, I recommend bringing an international license or obtaining an official translation of your Danish license, so you can drive around Australia (beware the kangaroos and the wombats on the road though).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships, travels in incredible Australia (especially diving at the coral reefs), meeting the engaging academic opportunity, and general life on campus

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The spiders (a lot do not really see them but I saw a lot...)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
